entertainment.title: LISA’s ‘Press Play’: All 6 Tracks Ranked
entertainment.summary: The global diva returns, relaxed and razor-sharp. Hit play, and a six-scene movie unfolds in your ears and behind your eyes.
entertainment.body:
On Sept. 27, LISA took home best pop at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards for “Dream,” beating a field that included Taylor Swift, Ariana Grande, Sabrina Carpenter and Olivia Rodrigo, and becoming the first K-pop soloist to win the category. It added to a run that already included a No. 7 peak on the Billboard 200 with last year’s Alter Ego . Then in September came pre-release single “SaWaDiKa,” which entered the Billboard Hot 100 at No. 69.

Now, with that momentum behind her, LISA unveils her new EP, Press Play . The title comes from a line on “Tarantino”: “It’s a movie baby, come and press play.” It’s a fitting name for a record that hits the eyes as hard as the ears. Press play and the scenes flash by: a tuk-tuk weaving through the streets of Bangkok, a Ferrari tearing around a circuit, a dance floor after midnight, a motel straight out of a Tarantino film, a yoga studio.

LISA holds a songwriting credit on every track, and Kuk Harrell, the vocal producer behind Rihanna’s “Umbrella,” worked on vocal production. Rap and sing-rap dominate much of the record, but each track carries its own texture, so it never drags.

The world should get ready for the movie LISA has brought with her. Below, Billboard Korea ranks all six tracks on Press Play .

“Cut U Off” opens with one of cinema’s most famous whistles: the tune Elle Driver whistles as she walks down a hospital corridor in a nurse’s uniform, on her way to kill the Bride in Quentin Tarantino’s Kill Bill: Vol. 1 (2003). Paired with LISA’s blade-sharp opening bars (“Chop chop,” “Master of sashimi”), it makes for a thrilling, suspenseful start.

LISA reframes the thrill of revenge at the heart of Kill Bill as the satisfaction of cutting someone off for good, delivering every line cool and unbothered. Past that striking intro, though, the track settles into easy-listening territory and doesn’t quite sustain the tension it opens with. Still, it’s a solid album cut that does its job.

entertainment.title: Hilary Duff Unwraps an Early Christmas Present With ‘Holiday Things’ EP: Steam It Now
entertainment.summary: In addition to a cover of the traditional "Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas," the mini-album features three originals.
entertainment.body:
Halloween candy hasn’t even been handed out yet, but Hilary Duff is definitely in a Christmas mood already. The singer-actress dropped the follow-up to this year’s sixth studio album of new material, Luck… or Something Friday (Oct. 23) with the five-track Yuletide EP Holiday Things . Explore Hilary Duff See latest videos, charts and news

The collection includes a cover of the holiday classic “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas,” as well as her updated version of Wham!’s beloved “Last Christmas,” which originally appeared on the singer’s 2002 debut studio album, Santa Claus Lane . Related Tate McRae Debuts at No. 1 In Australia With 'Housewife' LISA, Miley, Kacey Musgraves & John Mayer: New Music Friday Guide Cristian Castro Accepts the Billboard Lifetime Achievement Award 'In the Name of Romantic Love'

In addition, Holiday Things will feature three original tracks: “I Guess It’s Christmas,” “All You Want for Christmas Is Me” and “I Want (A Few Small Things).” In an Instagram post promoting the EP on Wednesday (Oct. 21), Duff teased, “I guess Christmas came early … Holiday Things is yours this Friday 10.23 ✨💝🥂,” alongside a picture of her looking glum at a party. In the snap, the frowning singer wears a fancy, frilly party dress as she sits in front of a forest of pink and blue balloons near a table festooned with a cake and champagne on ice.

Duff celebrated the 24th anniversary of Santa Claus Lane on Oct. 15, posting the cover of the album on Instagram alongside snaps of her three children with her husband, producer Matthew Koma, and throwback promo images from her teen star days.

After a decade-long retreat from releasing music, Duff has stormed back this year with Luck… or Something , which debuted at No. 3 on the Billboard 200 , followed up April by (Mine) , featuring re-recordings of such beloved Hot 100 hits as “Come Clean,” “What Dreams Are Made Of” and “Wake Up,” and then, earlier this month, “CATastrophe,” from The Cat in the Hat soundtrack.

Duff is gearing up for a run of sold-out shows in Australia kicking off on Saturday (Oct. 24) at Qudos Bank Arena in Sydney, followed by a quartet of iHeartRadio Jingle Ball shows in L.A., New York, Boston and Nashville in December, and a 2027 North American, European and South American tour that will keep her on the road through next November.

entertainment.title: ‘Nobody Wants This’ Creator Erin Foster Reacts to Adam Brody Saying He Supports “A Free Palestine”: “It’s Complicated”
entertainment.summary: In an interview with GQ, the actor previously said of the Israel-Gaza war, “Put me down as thinking it’s a genocide. Put me down as wanting a free Palestine.”
entertainment.body:
Logo text Nobody Wants This creator Erin Foster is sharing her opinion on Adam Brody recently telling GQ he is in support of “a free Palestine .”

During an upcoming appearance on the Not Skinny But Not Fat podcast, per Entertainment Weekly , Foster was asked by host Amanda Hirsch how she felt about the actor’s previous comments about the Israel-Gaza war.

“You know, it’s complicated. I think our work environment, our set is very similar to dinner tables around the world where people are having debate and discussion and disagreeing,” the series creator said. “While I love Adam, I also disagree with him, and that’s okay.” Related Stories TV 'Nobody Wants This' Season 3 Review: Kristen Bell and Adam Brody's Netflix Romance Levels Up but Can't Ditch Old Habits Lifestyle Sally Rooney's Books Pulled From U.K. Shelves Amid Controversy Over Palestine Action Support

“I think that as the creator of the show, all I can say is that I want our Jewish fans to know that I see you and I hear you and I understand how you feel,” Foster continued. “And the show has always been and always will be a love letter to Judaism. That is why I made this show. It’s because of how beautiful of an experience I’ve had becoming Jewish and being a Jewish person, and sitting here right now at this time in the world where there is almost zero positive representation of Jewish people, I think it’s so important to have that.”

“That being said, everyone is entitled to a different opinion than me. I can just tell you what I created this show for, what the intention of the show is,” Foster concluded.

During a September profile with GQ , Brody, who appears on the Netflix series as a rabbi, discussed his political activism, and was asked if he thinks Hollywood has gotten more conservative. “I guess outspokenly so, yes. … Between COVID, a second Trump term, Israel-Gaza, it’s really brought out some different beliefs that I was ignorant to, and then disheartened by.”

The O.C. actor was asked how Israel-Gaza has come up in his messaging, to which he responded, “Truthfully, it hasn’t. I have spoken a lot about it privately. I haven’t spoken much about it publicly.” When asked if he’d like to speak about the topic, The O.C. actor said, “Put me down as thinking it’s a genocide. Put me down as wanting a free Palestine.”

“It’s awful that it’s taken so much death and misery, but it does feel like it’s reaching a breaking point that it should have a while ago,” he added. “I’m hopeful that another administration can really do some good and correct some of these policies that are helping that situation be as awful as it is.”

entertainment.title: ‘Clayface’ Aims to Give DC Studios a Box Office Win as ‘You Can See Everything’ Stays Strong
entertainment.summary: Also debuting this weekend are 'Wildwood,' 'Klara and the Sun,' 'Wicker' and 'Ali G: Who Iz I?'
entertainment.body:
Logo text Clayface looks to give the DC Studios team a reason for a happy face in its opening weekend at the box office , although it will encounter competition from the second frame for A24’s You Can See Everything , which continues to get audiences pumped.

Warner Bros. projects a launch between $25 million and $30 million domestically for Clayface from more than 3,400 North American theaters, along with an additional $20 million to $25 million internationally. Director James Watkins’ $44 million-budgeted body-horror feature stars Tom Rhys Harries and Naomi Ackie in the story of Matt Hagen (Harries), an actor who turns to a scientist (Ackie) for assistance after his face becomes disfigured. Related Stories TV Jenna Ortega Says She'll Be "Off TV for Awhile" After 'Wednesday' Ends Movies 'Wildwood' Director Travis Knight on Spending 16 Years to Create His Stop-Motion "Masterpiece"

This marks the third feature release in the planned slate for DC Studios bosses James Gunn and Peter Safran. Superman kicked off the DC Universe’s film side with a strong start last year, while Supergirl sputtered over the summer, with the $170 million-budgeted movie debuting to a soft $37.1 million domestically before ending its run with $126 million worldwide. Clayface has the benefit of a far more modest budget.

Clayface has fared better with critics than Supergirl , holding a 75 percent approval from Rotten Tomatoes reviewers, as opposed to the 52 score for the summer’s Milly Alcock-led release. In his r e view for The Hollywood Reporter , critic Frank Scheck called Clayface “a big swing that definitely pays off.”

Offering potential competition for the weekend’s top spot is A24’s buzzy Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything , which expands to 2,600 North American theaters after playing in 855 in its debut frame. Directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim ‘s film about the disgraced Theranos founder’s life before beginning her prison sentence was a sensation in its opening weekend, overperforming to the tune of $15 million as it placed second behind Paramount and Legendary’s Street Fighter.

You Can See Everything is projected to gross at least $18 million for the weekend and could likely go beyond that.

Hitting theaters this weekend is Laika’s animated stop-motion feature Wildwood from director Travis Knight. It is set for 2,926 North American theaters and holds a sterling 100 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

entertainment.title: Michael Gray, Former Teen Idol and Star of ‘Shazam!,’ Dies at 75
entertainment.summary: After dating Marcia on ‘The Brady Bunch,’ he spent three seasons turning into Captain Marvel on Saturday mornings.
entertainment.body:
Michael Gray, who starred on the 1970s Saturday morning kids show Shazam! as Billy Batson, the teenager who in a puff of smoke turns into the superhero Captain Marvel , died Friday in Palm Desert of natural causes, a family spokesperson announced.

Gray frequently graced the covers of Tiger Beat and other popular teen magazines as he landed his first series gig as a student doctor named Ronnie Collins on the first season of the 1972-74 NBC sitcom The Little People , starring Brian Keith and Shelley Fabares .

Gray’s Billy had but to utter one word — “shazam” — to be transformed into Captain Marvel (played by Jackson Bostwick and then John Davey) on the live-action CBS show that aired for three seasons (1974-76). Watch the opening of the show here . Related Stories Movies Tom Skerritt, Star of 'Picket Fences' and 'Alien,' Dies at 93 News Ann Hornaday, Longtime Washington Post Film Critic, Dies at 66

“I remember when we were experimenting with the change from Billy to Captain Marvel, using a sort of flash device, and poof — the smoke would clear and I was a little singed,” Gray recalled in an interview with Comic Book Resources. “They changed that real quick. That definitely didn’t work.”

Gray then had a cameo in Shazam! Fury of the Gods (2023), where he interacted with Zachary Levi’s Captain Marvel in a nod to the original series.

Born in Chicago on Sept. 2, 1951, Gray was raised in Miami Beach before he headed to Hollywood, where he studied acting at the Pasadena Playhouse.

He made his onscreen debut on a 1969 episode of Room 222 , then showed up on The Flying Nun , Marcus Welby, M.D. and The Brady Bunch , where he played Marcia’s boyfriend on a 1973 installment (when she’s working in the local ice cream shop).

He also appeared in 1970 with Burt Reynolds in the ABC telefilm Run, Simon, Run and in the features Beyond the Valley of the Dolls and Myra Breckinridge .

Logo text Earlier Thursday, Prime Video announced a second season renewal for Carrie . Now there’s publicly available data backing up the decision.

Carrie premiered as the No. 1 streaming title in the United States for the week of Oct. 5-11. The eight-episode season, a present-day update of Stephen King’s novel from showrunner Mike Flanagan, racked up 1.26 billion viewing minutes for the week (the series debuted on Oct. 7).

Prime Video has been on a bit of a hot streak lately: It has had the No. 1 overall title six times in the past eight weeks of Nielsen’s streaming ratings . Reacher held the top ranking four times in August and September, giving way to spinoff Neagley in the week of Sept. 14-20 . Related Stories TV 'Carrie' Renewed for Second Season at Prime Video TV Josh Hartnett on Finding (and Shedding) His 'Below' Accent, and the Car Accident That Nearly Derailed Production

Also opening well in the Oct. 5-11 frame was Netflix’s Below . The thriller starring Josh Hartnett had 1.19 billion minutes of watch time, good for second overall. East of Eden grew by 49 percent week to week to 1.16 billion minutes, which put in third place.

The previous week’s top show, Wonka’s The Golden Ticket , fell off by 44 percent to 600 million viewing minutes for Netflix. It dropped out of the overall top 10 but finished sixth among original series. Ted Lasso (943 million minutes), on the other hand, scored a six-week high on Apple TV, coinciding with its season four finale on Oct. 7.

Two shows got a boost from licensing deals with Netflix: Paramount+’s Mayor of Kingstown (712 million minutes) and Disney+’s Percy Jackson and the Olympians (365 million) charted after their libraries debuted on Netflix (new seasons of both, in their original homes, will premiere in the next few months).
